lastCompletedStory.title: Fail closed when --headless meets container isolation

nextStoryContext: US-006 closed the last gap US-005's handoff flagged: headless (`opts.headless === true`) + `workerIsolation === 'container'` now fails closed BEFORE any dispatch. The check lives as the FIRST statement inside the existing `if (opts.headless === true) { ... }` branch in `loop.ts` (ahead of even the `headlessDispatchFn === undefined` throw), and mirrors the pre-existing `container-not-ready` early-return's fail-closed shape verbatim: `lastOutcome = { kind: 'blocked', storyId: undefined, detail: containerReason }`, `iterations++`, `removeImplementerTaskPrompt(uuid)`, best-effort `escalateFn()`, `finishTerminal('blocked')`, `return { status: 'blocked', iterations, lastOutcome }`. `containerReason` is `headless-container-unsupported: headless dispatch does not support workerIsolation === 'container' (advisory <storyId>)`, satisfying AC1's 'detail names both headless and container' requirement via substring match on both words. Deliberately does NOT touch host.ts: `workerIsolation` and `opts.headless` are both already resolved once (function-scope consts, `loop.ts` lines ~938 and read fresh per-tick via `opts.headless`), so the join-check belongs at the one branch point that consumes both, not as a third independently-resolved closure in host.ts. Because the guard runs before the `headlessDispatchFn === undefined` throw, a container-mode test never needs to wire a fake dispatch fn to prove unreachability. New test file `test/supervisor/headless-container-failclose.test.ts` (3 tests, mirrors `headless-route.test.ts`'s `makeBaseOpts` fixture shape): (1) blocks-before-dispatch with detail naming both axes, headlessDispatchFn never invoked, spawn never invoked; (2) `never wraps through docker exec` -- proof-by-absence, filters the injected spawn fake's recorded args for `'docker exec'` and asserts zero matches (this assertion would trivially pass even pre-fix, since the headless branch never built `dispatchCmd`/called `dockerExecWrap` regardless of the new guard -- the fail-closed VALUE this story adds is entirely in AC1's blocked-outcome + AC3's scoping, not in AC2 alone); (3) `host mode still dispatches` -- `workerIsolation: 'host'` + `headless: true` still calls `headlessDispatchFn` exactly once and completes normally, proving the guard is scoped to container only, not headless in general. All 6154 pre-existing tests plus these 3 new ones stayed green (6151 -> 6154). Ceiling raise this story made (single `_ref` note): `src/supervisor/loop.ts` 2902->2934. Gap intentionally left open for a future story (not required by this PRD's notes, flag if it becomes relevant): the review-dispatch path (`review.ts`, wired via `makeReviewDispatch` in host.ts) already threads `workerIsolation` for container-mode review dispatch, but has no headless route at all today (`headless`/`headlessDispatchFn` are implementer-only fields on `RunSupervisorOptions`); a future `--headless` story that extends to the reviewer phase will need its own container-compat decision, this story's guard does not cover it.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal control-flow guard (one early-return inside an existing if-branch in loop.ts) reusing an already-established fail-closed outcome shape. No new external library surface introduced or re-touched at the API-shape level.
